documents.why: s 8(2)(b) of the Bill: employment 'under the Members of Parliament (Staff) Act 1984 as a member of the staff of' listed office-holders. Needed: s 3 (office-holder, relevant office, personal employee, electorate employee), s 3AA, s 4 (determinations making a parliamentarian an office-holder), s 11 (employment powers). Earlier versions of the Act (before the 2023 amendments) are not pinned: see the reference register.

documents.why: not cited by the Bill, but it is the statute that shows who appoints heads of mission: s 39(1) ('The appointment of a Head of Mission by the Governor-General cannot take effect unless the person is an APS employee'), s 39(2) (Agency Minister's directions to engage a person or assign duties so the person can become a Head of Mission), s 7 ('Head of Mission' means the head of an Australian diplomatic or consular mission; 'Secretary' means the Secretary of a Department), s 25 (assignment of duties, the usual route for acting arrangements) and s 29 (termination of employment)

documents.title: Transparent and Quality Public Appointments Bill 2026 (Dr Sophie Scamps MP, private Member's Bill, House of Representatives, introduced 2 March 2026)
documents.retrieval_method: found by web search; the member's page refused scripted access (403); a local news report (https://www.pittwateronlinenews.com/Scamps-Ending-Jobs-for-Mates-Bill-March-2026.php) was read through WebFetch
documents.note: a general scheme for 'major' Commonwealth appointments, with independent selection panels and a cooling-off period of 6 months for former politicians and senior political staff and 18 months for former Ministers (per the news report). Whether it covers heads of mission, and its aph.gov.au bill id, are not known; its predecessor was the Transparent and Quality Public Appointments Bill 2023 (bId r6981). For the human at 3H.
